about: Roboteer fight commentary (wave D). Original lines only: no show names, no presenter or commentator catchphrases (brief v3 section 3). Every line fires only when its facts are true: a {placeholder} needs that fact, and 'if' lists more (flag, !flag, key=value, !key=value). 'w' is a weight (default 10), 'p' the priority (0 filler .. 3 payoff and result), 'cool' the seconds before the same key (per 'per' when set) may fire again, 'life' how long it may wait for the ticker, 'group' a set of keys only one of which is said per fight.

prediction.doc: Before the bell. attacker = the machine the facts favour (or the player's when even), victim = the other, weapon = attacker's. Flags: even, favourite, armour_edge, record_edge, same_weapon, spin_vs_lift, rematch, house.

lines.t: Nothing between {attacker} and {victim} on paper. Paper won't help either of them.
{attacker} against {victim}. I tossed a coin twice and it landed on its edge.
Evenly matched, they tell me. One of them will be less even shortly.
Hard to call this one. I'll be calling it very loudly all the same.
{attacker} or {victim}? My heart says one, my notes say the other.
Two {weapon}s in the same arena. Somebody's going to feel copied.
Mirror match. {weapon} against {weapon}, last reflection standing.
Same weapon, different ideas. Both of them brought the {weapon}.
{attacker} carries the thicker plate. {victim} will have to find a gap.
More armour on {attacker}. {victim} has brought the tin opener, I hope.
{attacker} is built like a post box. {victim} needs to post something through it.
{attacker} comes in with the better record. Form is lovely until it isn't.
The numbers favour {attacker}. {victim} has never cared much for numbers.
My money's on {attacker}. Not much money, mind.
{attacker} starts as favourite. {victim} has read that and taken it personally.
{attacker} wants to hit. {victim} wants to lift. First to do it gets the evening.
{victim} must get underneath before {attacker}'s {weapon} gets going.
These two have met before, and nobody in the pits has forgotten.
{attacker} and {victim} again. Unfinished business, and some finished business.
{house_bot} is in the corner tonight. Stay out of it if you like your paintwork.
And keep an eye on {house_bot} in the corner. It's keeping an eye on you.

lines: {attacker} against {victim}. Let's see what all those workshop hours were for.
Welcome to {arena}. {attacker} and {victim}, and one of them won't enjoy it.
{attacker} versus {victim}. Everybody has a plan until the first hit.

walkout_player.doc: The player's machine through the gate. attacker = the machine, weapon = its weapon.
lines: Here comes {attacker}, and the crowd are on their feet.
{attacker} rolls out of the gate. Freshly painted, briefly.
Out comes {attacker}, {weapon} and all.
{attacker} through the gate. It's had a wash for this.
Big cheer for {attacker}. Well, a cheer. It's definitely a cheer.
{attacker} arrives with its {weapon} and its fingers crossed.
{attacker} is out. Somebody's been up all night with a spanner.
The home workshop's finest. Give it up for {attacker}!

walkout_opponent.doc: The opponent through the gate. attacker = the machine, weapon = its weapon.
lines: And in the other corner, {attacker}. It's brought its {weapon}.
Here's {attacker}. The scouts say it bites.
{attacker} rolls out to a few boos. It seems to enjoy them.
{attacker} now, and it has the look of a machine with plans.
Out comes {attacker}. I wouldn't lend it anything.
The opposition, {attacker}, {weapon} to the fore.
{attacker} through the gate. Mean looking thing, isn't it?

fight_start.doc: The bell (after 3, 2, 1, FIGHT). attacker = the player's machine, victim = the opponent.
lines: And we're off!
Here we go, then. {attacker} against {victim}.
Away they go!
It's under way in {arena}!
Lights go, wheels go. Here we are.
And they're moving. Game on.
Off they go, and nobody's hanging about.
Power down! That's your lot.
And that's it. Power down, everybody.
Power down. Somebody put the kettle on.
That's the end of that. Weapons off, please.
Power down, and breathe.

first_blood.doc: The first real blow between the two machines. attacker/victim/weapon (attacker's). Flags: wk=<kind>, spin_weapon, src_burn.
lines: First blood to {attacker}!
{attacker} draws first blood. Well, first oil.
{attacker} lands the first one, and {victim} felt it.
There's the first contact, and it's {attacker} who made it.
{attacker} opens the account against {victim}.
First dent of the fight goes to {attacker}.
First blood to {attacker}'s {weapon}.

lines.t: {attacker} gets the spinner into {victim} first. That's drawn blood.

big_hit.doc: A blow at the FX layer's heavy severity. attacker/victim/weapon (attacker's). Flags: wk=<kind>, spin_weapon, src_burn, house (attacker is the house bot), attacker=<name>, victim=<name>.

lines.t: What a hit from {attacker}!

lines: Oh, {victim} felt that one!

lines.t: {attacker} absolutely clatters {victim}!
That's a proper wallop from {attacker}.

lines: Big hit! {victim} will want a lie down after that.

lines.t: Crunch! {attacker} means business.
Oh, I say. {attacker} has hit {victim} very hard indeed.

lines: Somewhere a mechanic just winced. Big hit on {victim}.

lines.t: {attacker} lands a haymaker!

lines: That's gone right through {victim}'s afternoon.

lines.t: Take that! A thumping blow from {attacker}.
Heavy, heavy hit from {attacker}.
{victim} is rattling. {attacker} is not a bit sorry.
Wallop! {victim} will be feeling that one in the morning.
{attacker}'s {weapon} bites and {victim} goes skipping across the floor!
Spinner connects! {victim} bounces like a dropped tea tray.
All that stored energy in one place, and the place is {victim}.
The {weapon} sings and {victim} pays the bill.
{attacker} brings the axe down like it's chopping firewood.
Timber! The axe lands square on {victim}.
Axe to the lid of {victim}. Knock knock, who's there? Pain.
{attacker} gets the claw in and squeezes!
That's a crushing handshake from {attacker}.
{attacker} carves into {victim}. Sparks everywhere!
The saw's in, and {victim} is being sliced like the Sunday roast.
{attacker} runs straight through {victim}. Route one football, that.
{attacker} drills in. {victim} is being renovated.
{victim} is getting toasted by {attacker}.
Hot, hot, hot! {attacker} turns up the gas on {victim}.
{attacker} gives {victim} a jolt. Hair on end, if it had hair.
{attacker} arcs into {victim}. Crackle and pop!
{house_bot} smashes into {victim}!
{house_bot} lands one on {victim}. Nobody asked it to.
{house_bot} does what {house_bot} does, and {victim} pays for it.
GRUDGE never forgets, and {victim} won't forget this either.
ANVIL comes down on {victim} like, well, an anvil.
CINDER gets {victim} very hot under the collar.
BANDSAW takes a slice out of {victim}.
THRESHER threshes, and {victim} is the harvest.
Clatterbox lives up to its name. What a clatter!
Clatterbox is clattering, and not the way it meant to.
Hob Nail hits it right on the head!
Hob Nail gets hammered for a change.
Penny Dread makes it count. Every penny.
That one will cost Penny Dread a lot more than a penny.
The brass neck on Brass Neck! Straight in.
Brass Neck takes one on the chin. A brass chin, luckily.
Cold Snap snaps, and {victim} gets the shivers.
Cold Snap gets a very warm welcome from {attacker}.
Tollgate collects! {victim} pays in full.
That's a toll Tollgate did not want to pay.
Scuttle scuttles in and bites!
Scuttle's been scuttled! Well, dented.
Marrow gets its teeth into {victim}. Chilled to the marrow.
Marrow felt that one right down in the marrow.
Tinribs takes one in the ribs. Tin ones, thankfully.

part_off.doc: A real part came off (armour plate, wheel). part = its name, victim = its owner, attacker = who did it when a machine did. Flags: part_wheel, part_armour, part_top, part_face, hazard, house.
lines: There goes {victim}'s {part}!

lines.t: {attacker} has knocked the {part} clean off {victim}!
The {part} is off! {attacker} is taking {victim} apart.

lines: {victim} is losing bits. That's the {part} on the floor.

lines.t: {attacker} rips the {part} away. That'll need more than glue.

lines: The {part} has left the building. {victim} carries on without it.
Bits everywhere! {victim}'s {part} is gone.

lines.t: {attacker} takes the {part} as a souvenir.

lines: Look at that, {victim}'s {part} bouncing across the floor.
Somebody fetch a bucket. {victim} has dropped its {part}.

lines.t: A wheel's gone from {victim}! That'll change the handling.
Wheel off! {victim}'s {part} is rolling away on its own.
{victim}'s {part} is making a break for it.
The lid's off {victim}! You can see the wiring.
{victim}'s lid has gone. Mind the insides, everyone.
That's {victim}'s {part} gone. It's naked on that side now.
The arena takes {victim}'s {part}, and the floor is keeping it.
{victim} leaves its {part} in the hazard. Donation received.
{house_bot} tears the {part} off {victim}. Uninvited and unhelpful.
{house_bot} takes {victim}'s {part} home as a trophy.

pinned.doc: A pin that has held 0.6 s. attacker = the machine holding, victim = the one pinned.
lines: {attacker} has {victim} pinned!
{victim} is held down, and {attacker} isn't letting go.
Pinned! {victim} is going nowhere for the moment.
{attacker} leans on {victim}. That's a very heavy hug.
{victim} is trapped. Wriggle, {victim}, wriggle!
{attacker} parks on {victim}. No ticket required.
That's a pin from {attacker}. {victim} is running out of room.
{victim} wants to leave. {attacker} has other ideas.

flipped.doc: A machine has gone upside down. victim = it. attacker = the machine that touched it inside 1.5 s, if any. Flags: self (nobody near), wk=<attacker's kind>, house.
lines: {victim} is upside down!
Over goes {victim}!
{victim} is showing us its underside.

lines.t: {attacker} flips {victim} over!
Over goes {victim}! Lovely work from {attacker}.
{victim} is on its back, and {attacker} did that.
Upside down! {attacker} turns {victim} turtle.
{attacker} gets underneath and {victim} goes over. Textbook.
Belly up for {victim}. {attacker} is delighted.
The flipper fires and {victim} takes flight!
{attacker} launches {victim}. Air miles for {victim}!
{attacker} lifts and tips {victim} over like a wheelbarrow.
{house_bot} tips {victim} over. Charming.
{victim} has flipped itself over! Nobody touched it!
Oh dear. {victim} has turned itself upside down all on its own.
{victim} goes over without any help at all. Embarrassing.
Nobody near it and {victim} is on its roof. You couldn't make it up.

self_right.doc: An inverted machine is back upright. victim = it.
lines: {victim} is back on its wheels. Crisis over.
Up it gets! {victim} rights itself.
{victim} pops back over. Lovely bit of engineering, that.
Back the right way up, {victim}. As you were.
{victim} shrugs it off and gets back upright.
And {victim} is up. Dusts itself down, carries on.

spinning_up.doc: A spinner, drum, full body spinner or saw has reached full speed. attacker = its owner, weapon = it. Flags: wk=<kind>, spin_weapon.

lines.t: {attacker}'s {weapon} is up to speed. Mind your fingers.
Hear that whine? That's {attacker} getting ready.
{attacker} is spun up and looking for customers.
The {weapon} on {attacker} is at full chat.
{attacker} has wound itself right up. Nasty.
Full speed on {attacker}'s {weapon}. Nobody stand near that.
That drum on {attacker} is humming like a tumble dryer.
{attacker}'s saw is screaming. Somebody's going to get sliced.
{attacker}'s saw is up to speed. Carving knife out.

spin_lost.doc: A spun-up weapon has fallen back below the AI's spun-down line. attacker = its owner, victim = the other machine, weapon = it. Flags: after_hit (it was in a blow inside 0.6 s), spin_weapon, wk=<kind>.
lines: {attacker}'s {weapon} has lost its speed. Now's the moment, {victim}!
{attacker} is spinning down. {victim} should get in there.
The {weapon} on {attacker} is winding down. Opportunity knocks.
{attacker}'s {weapon} slows right off. It'll need a moment.

lines.t: That hit has cost {attacker} its spin. Window open for {victim}.
{attacker} gave it everything and the {weapon} is spent. Go on, {victim}!

weapon_jammed.doc: A weapon has reached zero and jammed for the rest of the fight. victim = its owner, weapon = it. Flags: player. Once per machine.
lines: {victim}'s {weapon} has packed up. It's a pusher now.
Nothing coming from {victim}'s {weapon}. That's broken.
{victim} has lost its {weapon}. It'll have to box clever.
The {weapon} on {victim} is dead. Somebody in the pits is swearing quietly.
{victim} presses the button and nothing happens. Oh dear.
No more {weapon} for {victim}. Wheels and wits from here.

lines.t: That's {victim}'s {weapon} finished. Time to drive, not fight.

weapon_cooked.doc: A flame has knocked a weapon's electrics out for a while. victim = its owner, weapon = it.
lines: {victim}'s electrics are cooked. The {weapon} is sulking.
The heat's got into {victim}. Its {weapon} has gone quiet for a bit.
{victim} is too hot to fight properly. Give it a moment.
Flames in the wiring, and {victim}'s {weapon} has stopped answering.

in_the_zone.doc: The player's machine has driven into the house bot's corner. victim = it, house_bot.
lines: {victim} has wandered into {house_bot}'s corner. Brave. Daft, but brave.
Oh no, {victim}, not in there! That's {house_bot}'s patch.
{victim} is in the corner, and {house_bot} is licking its lips.
Wrong corner, {victim}! {house_bot} has been waiting for you.
{victim} knocks on {house_bot}'s door. Someone is home.
{victim} is trespassing. {house_bot} takes that very seriously.

house_bot_out.doc: The house bot is on the floor. house_bot. Flags: endgame (released at the endgame), idle (sent in because nobody was fighting).
lines: {house_bot} is on the floor!
And {house_bot} joins the party.

lines.t: {house_bot} is out of its corner! Everybody look busy.
Here comes {house_bot}. The last stretch just got crowded.
They've let {house_bot} out. Things are about to get unfair.
{house_bot} is on the prowl. Nobody is safe now.
The corner opens and {house_bot} rolls out looking for trouble.
Nobody's fighting, so {house_bot} will. In it comes!
Too quiet for {house_bot}'s liking. Out it comes to stir things up.
That's what you get for dawdling. {house_bot} is coming in.

pit_open.doc: Drop Zone's endgame: the pit opens.
lines: The pit is open! Mind your step.
Hole in the floor, everybody! The pit is open.
Down goes the floor. Nobody wants to be first in.
The pit's open for business. Customers wanted.
That's the pit open. Suddenly the arena feels a lot smaller.

endgame.doc: The endgame, in an arena without a pit and without a house bot (its release says the endgame when there is one).
lines: Endgame! This is where it gets serious.
Into the endgame. Anything left in the tank, now's the time.
Endgame. Last chance saloon for somebody.
We're into the endgame. Hold on to your hats.
The endgame's here, and the crowd have found their voices.
Final stretch. Nobody wants to leave this to the judges.
Hazards up! The floor has joined the fight.
The hazards are live. Watch where you're driving.
{arena} comes to life. Everything in here bites now.
Hazards on! Somebody is going to find out the hard way.
The arena's awake now. Tread carefully, both of you.
Hazards are live. Suddenly the floor has opinions.

stage_wake.doc: Stage 2, the arena's own wake word. arena, word. Flags: arena=<id>.

lines.t: The grinders are awake in the Yard. Keep your wheels clear.
Grinders on! The Yard just grew teeth.
Hear those grinders? That's the Yard getting hungry.
The spikes are awake! Mind the floor.
Up come the spikes. As if the Grinder wasn't sharp enough already.
Spikes live! Nobody wants to park on those.
The spikes are awake in the Crush. Rams above, pins below.
Spikes as well as rams now. The Crush is showing off.
The pit stays open from here. No more second chances.
That pit's open for good now. Edge of the seat, edge of the hole.
The side jets are lit! It's getting warm in the Furnace.
More flame down the sides. The Furnace lives up to its name.
The discs are spinning up in the Coliseum! Stay off them.
Spinning discs in the floor now. The Coliseum wants a show.
The arena has woken up properly now.

stage_final.doc: The final stage (25 s left). arena, word. Flags: arena=<id>.

lines.t: The rams are going nonstop now! Nowhere is safe.
Rams on repeat! The Crush is in a terrible mood.
Final seconds! Everything's live.
The last push. The arena is at full throttle.
Into the final seconds. Win it now or hand it to the judges.

last_ten.doc: Ten seconds left on the clock.
lines: Ten seconds left! Last orders!
Ten to go. Anybody got anything left?
Final ten seconds! Throw everything at it!
Ten seconds. This is where legends are made, or dented.
Ten seconds on the clock. Go on!

comeback.doc: A machine that was 20 %+ behind on condition has drawn level or gone ahead. attacker = the comer, victim = the other. Once per machine.
lines: {attacker} was on the ropes and now look at it!
What a comeback from {attacker}! {victim} was well on top not long ago.
{attacker} has clawed it back! Level on condition.
Don't write off {attacker}! It's all square again.
From battered to level. {attacker} will not lie down.
{attacker} has turned this round! Who saw that coming?
The fightback is on! {attacker} is right back in this.
{attacker} was held together with tape a minute ago. Now it's level!

stall.doc: 8 s or more with no contact and no blow. attacker/victim = the two machines, seconds = how long. Flags: apart (more than 3 m apart).
lines: Plenty of looking, not much touching.
Come on, somebody do something!
It's gone a bit quiet. I could make a cup of tea.
Lovely driving. Now could they hit each other, please?
This is a stand-off. The crowd would like a stand-on.
Bit of a chess match, this. Without the pieces moving.
The crowd paid for a fight, not a car park.
I've seen more aggression at a garden centre.
Nobody wants to go first. Very polite. Very dull.
Somebody tell them the clock is running.

lines.t: {attacker} and {victim} are admiring each other from a distance.
They're circling. Somebody commit!
{seconds} seconds without a touch. The crowd are checking their phones.

hazard_self.doc: A machine hurt by the arena with nobody in contact inside 3 s: it drove there itself. victim = it.
lines: {victim} has driven into the hazard all by itself!
Nobody pushed {victim}. It went in there on its own.
Oh dear, {victim}. That hazard was clearly marked.
{victim} finds the hazard without any help. Brave, or lost?
Self-inflicted! {victim} drives straight into trouble.
Unforced error from {victim}. The arena says thank you.
{victim} has had a navigational mishap. A painful one.
Did {victim} not see that? It certainly felt it.

stuck.doc: The arena's unstick nudge: a machine wedged on the scenery, away from its opponent. victim = it.
lines: {victim} is stuck on the scenery. Somebody give it a shove.
{victim} has wedged itself. Wheels spinning, going nowhere.
Oh, {victim} is caught on something. The arena helps it out.
{victim} is beached! Hang on, there, it's free.
Stuck fast, {victim}. There we go, a little nudge.
{victim} has parked itself on the furniture.

wedge_under.doc: A wedge chassis in contact with the other machine, which is lifted off the floor and upright. attacker = the wedge, victim = the lifted one.
lines: {attacker} gets the wedge underneath {victim}!
Under it goes! {attacker}'s wedge has {victim} up on its toes.
{victim} is riding up {attacker}'s ramp. Wheels off the floor!
{attacker} slides underneath. {victim} has lost its grip.
Lovely low driving from {attacker}. {victim} is up in the air.
That wedge is doing its job. {victim} is on the ramp.

lockup_tow.doc: The Marshal tows two locked machines apart. attacker/victim = the two.
lines: The Marshal steps in and pulls {attacker} and {victim} apart.
Locked together, so the Marshal tows them apart. Separate corners!
Too friendly by half. The Marshal parts {attacker} and {victim}.
Break! The Marshal untangles the pair of them.
The Marshal separates them. Nobody was getting anywhere.
Tangled up, and here's the Marshal with the tow line.

count_start.doc: The Marshal starts a knockout count on an immobile machine. victim = it.
lines: {victim} isn't moving. The Marshal starts the count.
Count's on for {victim}! Come on, move!
The Marshal is counting {victim}. Wriggle, anything!
{victim} has stopped. Here comes the count.
{victim} is sitting still and the lights are counting down.

count_out.doc: The count reaches the end. victim = the machine counted out, attacker = the winner.
lines: {victim} is counted out!
And that's the count. {victim} is out.
The count's done. {victim} couldn't beat it.
Counted out! {victim} has nothing left.
{victim} goes the full count. That's that.

fire_out.doc: The Marshal sprays out a fire. victim = the machine it sprays.
lines: The Marshal puts {victim} out. Well, the fire on it.
Bit of smoke on {victim}. The Marshal gives it a spray.
Out with the extinguisher. {victim} is fine. Ish.
The Marshal hoses down {victim}. Lovely and cool.
{victim} was on fire. Now it's merely damp.

marshal_wobble.doc: The Marshal drone takes a knock and wobbles.
lines: The Marshal takes a knock and wobbles. Somebody steady it.
Oh, the Marshal's had a wobble. Keep it together, officer.
Poor Marshal. That was not in the job description.
The Marshal goes a bit wonky. Still counting, though.
Easy, Marshal. We need you upright.

house_finish.doc: After the result: the house bot's finishing ritual on the loser. house_bot, victim. Flags: hazard (it shoves the loser into a hazard).
lines: {house_bot} isn't finished with {victim}. Oh, that's unkind.
And {house_bot} comes to collect what's left of {victim}.
{house_bot} gives {victim} the send-off. No flowers.
Kicking a machine when it's down. {house_bot}, honestly.
It's over, {house_bot}! Leave it alone!
{house_bot} makes sure {victim} knows it lost.

lines.t: {house_bot} shoves {victim} into the hazard. Just to be sure.
{house_bot} tidies {victim} away into the hazard. Charming.

house_late_hit.doc: After the result: the house bot lands a late hit. house_bot, victim.
lines: That was after the bell! Disgraceful, {house_bot}!
{house_bot}! The fight is over! Somebody tell it!
Oh, that's a late one from {house_bot}. Cheap shot on {victim}.
After the bell! {house_bot}, you absolute rotter.
Outrageous! {house_bot} lands one on {victim} after the result.
Did {house_bot} not hear the bell? I think it heard the bell.
That's not on, {house_bot}. That is really not on.

house_card.doc: The Marshal cards the house bot. house_bot.
lines: The Marshal shows {house_bot} a card. {house_bot} does not care.
Card for {house_bot}! As if that'll help.

judges.doc: The bell with both still going: it goes to the judges. attacker/victim = the two.
lines: That's time, and it goes to the judges.
Nobody finished it, so the judges will. Over to them.
All the way to the bell. The judges have homework.

verdict_clear.doc: A clear judges' decision (margin over 2 points of 10). attacker = the winner, victim = the loser, margin.
lines: The judges go for {attacker}, and nobody's arguing.
{attacker} takes it on the cards. Clear as day.
A clear decision for {attacker}. Well earned.
{attacker} wins it, and the crowd agree.
No doubts there. {attacker} gets the verdict.
{attacker} on points, and comfortably.

verdict_close.doc: A close judges' decision (margin 2 points or under). attacker = the winner, victim = the loser, margin.
lines: {attacker} edges it! Hear the crowd, they're not happy.

knockout.doc: A knockout. attacker = the winner, victim = the machine knocked out. Flags: inverted (it ended upside down).

That's the end of {victim}. Knockout to {attacker}!

payoff_spikes.doc: A machine shoved onto the spikes (credited). attacker = who did it, victim.
